# Langfuse #15208: score analytics silently report wrong values

- Status at capture: open
- Upstream: https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/15208
- Pinned source: `langfuse@c4eaf1f4c0cd1851f0c9dbea2802c243cf787a09`

Two dashboard analytics functions silently return incorrect results.
`createHistogramData` rounds fractional scores before selecting a bin, so a
value can be counted outside the range printed on its bucket. Pivot-table
subtotals and grand totals compute an unweighted mean of already aggregated
group averages, which is wrong when group sizes differ.

Acceptance criteria:

1. A regression case places `0.857` in the correct bucket for seven bins over
   `[0, 1]`; rounding is limited to display labels.
2. Average subtotals use row counts as weights when a count metric exists and
   retain a documented fallback when it does not.
3. Existing integer-score and non-average aggregations remain unchanged.
4. Focused tests cover both analytics paths.

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_aca3c58497ec4182b8df9c0d6f2e9f89",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/ensemble-eval-orchestration-and-weighting-guidelines-2026.json",
    "title": "Ensemble evaluation orchestration and weighting guidelines",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Ensemble evaluation orchestration and weighting guidelines\",\n  \"space\": \"applied-ml-and-evals\",\n  \"author\": \"Priya Menon\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Liam Chen\",\n    \"Sofia Alvarez\",\n    \"Jonas Becker\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"eval-harness\",\n    \"ensemble\",\n    \"quality-guardrails\",\n    \"scoring\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/continuous-safety-eval-pipeline-and-integration-guide-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/workload-transferability-and-quant-benchmarks-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Overview\\n=======\\n\\nPurpose\\n-------\\nThis document specifies a standard for orchestrating ensemble-style evaluations in Redwood's eval harness. It covers how to configure multi-metric evaluation jobs, how to compute a single acceptance score from heterogeneous metrics, recommended weighting strategies, and the operational rules used for model acceptance, canary rollouts, and automated rollback triggers. The goal is consistent, explainable production decisions across different product use-cases (chat, summarization, reranking, embeddings).\\n\\nBackground and motivation\\n-------------------------\\nTeams frequently need to combine multiple eval signals (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE-like n-gram overlap, semantic similarity, safety pass rate, latency percentiles) into a single decision for model promotion or rollback. Without a standard approach:\\n- teams create ad-hoc weights that are hard to justify\\n- comparisons across workloads are inconsistent\\n- drift or slice regressions are missed when only aggregate metrics are considered\\n\\nScope\\n-----\\nThis guide applies to:\\n- All evaluation jobs run through eval-harness-runner and eval-orch services.\\n- Post-training checks that feed Redwood Optimize and model-onboarding pipelines.\\n- Production acceptance gates tied to rollout automation in the deployment orchestration layer.\\n\\nTerminology\\n-----------\\n- eval job: a single run that produces a set of metrics for a model version on a prompt set.\\n- slice: an orthogonal data subset (e.g., low-resource queries, long-contexts, legal-phrasing).\\n- metric vector: the set of scalar metrics produced by one eval job.\\n- ensemble score: a normalized, weighted aggregation of metrics used for acceptance decisions.\\n\\nHigh-level orchestration\\n-----------------------\\n1) Eval job submission: developers submit an eval job YAML to eval-orch. Jobs declare model id, dataset id, slices, metrics, and desired aggregations.\\n2) Parallel runners: eval-harness-runner scales horizontally to execute slices in parallel. Per-slice results are written to metric-store with a unique job id.\\n3) Post-processing: a standardized post-processing step normalizes raw metrics, computes slice-level z-scores or bounded transforms, and produces the ensemble score.\\n4) Decision hooks: the ensemble score is compared against the configured acceptance matrix (thresholds and weights). If the score passes, the model progresses to canary rollout; otherwise it triggers triage.\\n\\nOrchestration diagram (text)\\n---------------------------\\n- user -> eval-orch -> queue (kafka) -> runner pool -> metric-store (timeseries + artifacts) -> postproc -> decision-service -> deployment-orch\\n\\nWeighting and aggregation strategies\\n----------------------------------\\nWe provide three canonical strategies. Choose the simplest that satisfies your product requirements; prefer reproducibility over complexity.\\n\\n1) Equal-weight normalized aggregation (default)\\n- Use when metrics are commensurate after normalization (e.g., all are percentages or bounded scores).\\n- Steps: compute per-metric min/max clipped to historical percentiles (5th/95th), rescale to [0,1], average.\\n- Pros: simple, transparent.\\n- Cons: can under- or over-emphasize rare but critical metrics.\\n\\n2) Priority-weighted aggregation\\n- Use when one metric is safety-critical (e.g., toxicity, hallucination rate).\\n- Steps: assign integer priority weights (example: safety=5, accuracy=3, latency=1), normalize weights to sum to 1, compute weighted sum of normalized metrics.\\n- Documentation: every priority weight must have an author and justification recorded in the eval job metadata.\\n\\n3) Dynamic frequency-weighted aggregation (recommended for customer-facing embeddings/reranking)\\n- Use when production slice frequencies differ significantly from training/test distributions.\\n- Steps: estimate slice frequencies from production telemetry (last 30 days), compute per-slice weight proportional to frequency, and combine slice-level metric aggregates into a global metric before normalization.\\n- Important: frequency estimates are clipped to [0.01, 0.5] per slice to avoid domination by a single slice.\\n\\nNormalization and transforms\\n---------------------------\\nWe standardize on the following transforms before aggregation:\\n- bounded metrics in [0,1] (no transform)\\n- unbounded error metrics (e.g., MSE): apply inverse transform 1/(1+log(1+value)) then rescale to [0,1]\\n- latency percentiles: map P50/P95 to score = 1 - min(latency / latency_slo, 1) (SLOs stored in product-config)\\n- safety/failure rates: use 1 - rate so higher is better\\n- For metrics with heavy tails, use winsorization at 99th percentile prior to normalization\\n\\nScoring formula (canonical)\\n--------------------------\\nGiven normalized metrics m_i in [0,1] and weights w_i that sum to 1:\\nensemble_score = sum_i w_i * m_i\\n\\nWhen combining slices, compute slice_score_j first (per-slice aggregation across metrics), then global_score = sum_j slice_weight_j * slice_score_j where slice_weight_j is chosen per weighting strategy.\\n\\nConfig examples\\n--------------\\nExample eval job YAML (submit to eval-orch):\\n\\n---\\njob_name: \\\"chat-v2-ensemble-eval\\\"\\nmodel_id: \\\"m-redwood-chat-v2-2026-03\\\"\\ndataset_id: \\\"chat-production-sim-2026-01\\\"\\nmetrics: [\\\"semantic-similarity\\\", \\\"toxicity_rate\\\", \\\"response_length_variance\\\", \\\"p95_latency_ms\\\"]\\nslices: [\\\"all\\\", \\\"long_context_>2048\\\", \\\"low_english_proficiency\\\"]\\nweighting_strategy: \\\"dynamic-frequency\\\"\\nweights: {} # optional for dynamic; required for priority-weighted\\npostproc:\\n  normalization: \\\"percentile-clip-5-95\\\"\\n  latency_slo_ms: 150\\nnotify_on_fail: [\\\"ml-evals@redwoodeval.internal\\\"]\\n---\\n\\nExample postproc snippet (pseudo-YAML) for priority-weighted:\\n\\nweights:\\n  semantic-similarity: 0.4\\n  toxicity_rate: 0.4\\n  p95_latency_ms: 0.2\\nnormalization: \\\"1/(1+log(1+value))\\\"\\n\\nAcceptance matrix and thresholds\\n--------------------------------\\nAcceptance matrices must be checked into model-onboarding metadata and include:\\n- minimum safety pass rate by slice (e.g., safety >= 0.995 on all slices),\\n- global ensemble_score threshold (default 0.82),\\n- latency SLO tolerances (P95 <= configured SLO),\\n- allowed per-metric regressions from baseline (e.g., no more than 2% drop in semantic-similarity).\\n\\nDefault baseline policy (applies if team does not provide custom matrix):\\n- safety pass rate >= 0.998 on all slices\\n- ensemble_score >= 0.80\\n- no metric regressions > 3% compared to production baseline\\n- canary rollout limited to 5% traffic for 48 hours with monitoring hooks\\n\\nCanary and rollback rules\\n------------------------\\nCanary rollout: on pass, deployment-orch will deploy model to canary cluster at 5% traffic. During canary the following automated checks run every 15 minutes:\\n- Production sampler run: compare online metrics with eval predictions for a random sample of requests (1 per 1000 requests or at least 1000 samples/day).\\n- Alert conditions: ensemble_score drop > 0.05 vs baseline OR safety failure spike > 0.01 absolute OR P95 latency increase > 25% -> trigger rollback.\\n\\nAutomated rollback sequence (executed by deployment-orch):\\n1) Pause canary traffic.\\n2) Demote model from canary and switch traffic to previous stable model.\\n3) Create incident and assign to on-call owner of model-service (see runbooks).\\n4) Persist failing eval artifacts and logs under job id for triage.\\n\\nRegression triage flow\\n---------------------\\n1) Triage owner reviews per-slice deltas and pulls failing examples (eval-harness provides direct links).\\n2) If failure is dataset-related (label drift), tag dataset and schedule augmentation.\\n3) If failure is model-related (systematic hallucination/safety), open ModelRegression ticket with: baseline artifacts, counterexamples, per-slice metrics, and suggested mitigation (prompt tuning, quantization rollback, smaller context window).\\n4) For performance regressions, check runtime config (quantization profile, batching settings) and revert to last-known-good profile if needed.\\n\\nOperational considerations and do's/don'ts\\n----------------------------------------\\nDo:\\n- Record weight justifications in job metadata.\\n- Use production frequency data for dynamic weighting when available.\\n- Always include safety metrics as separate slices (do not absorb safety into a single aggregate without explicit weight).\\n- Keep acceptance matrices in model-onboarding for auditability.\\nDon't:\\n- Hard-code weights in deployment scripts without provenance.\\n- Use raw latency numbers directly without mapping to SLO-based scores.\\n- Rely solely on aggregate scores; always require per-slice checks for safety and critical business slices.\\n\\nMetrics and observability\\n------------------------\\n- metric-store: stores per-job, per-slice metrics with job_id and model_id tags.\\n- dashboards: ensemble-over-time, per-slice-breakdown, canary-sampler-comparison.\\n- alerts: configured in deployment-orch and routed to ml-evals and eng-sre channels.\\n\\nOwnership and SLAs\\n------------------\\n- Eval orchestration (eval-orch, runner): team = applied-ml (owner: Priya Menon).\\n- Post-processing & scoring library: team = applied-ml, SLAs for processing of a single job <= 30 minutes for medium datasets (<=100k examples).\\n- Decision-service and deployment hooks: team = eng-platform.\\n\\nRequired artifacts for onboarding a new model using ensemble evals\\n----------------------------------------------------------------\\n- eval job YAML and historical weight justifications (checked into model PR)\\n- acceptance matrix (JSON) checked into model-onboarding metadata store\\n- baseline production metrics snapshot (timestamped)\\n- list of critical slices and slice definitions\\n\\nAppendix: example of normalized score calculations\\n------------------------------------------------\\nGiven metrics: semantic_sim=0.78 (higher better), toxicity_rate=0.002 (lower better), p95_latency_ms=120 (SLO=150)\\nTransform toxicity: 1 - toxicity_rate = 0.998\\nTransform latency: 1 - min(120/150, 1) = 0.2\\nAssume weights [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] -> ensemble_score = 0.5*0.78 + 0.3*0.998 + 0.2*0.2 = 0.39 + 0.2994 + 0.04 = 0.7294\\n\\nLinks and references\\n--------------------\\n- eval-harness-runner README: internal link (eval-harness-runner)\\n- model-onboarding checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/production-model-certification-checklist-2026\\n- regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026\\n\\nContact and escalation\\n----------------------\\nFor questions about weighting strategy or to request new slice definitions, open an issue in the Applied-ML backlog and assign to the evals owner (Priya Menon). For production incidents related to canary rollouts, follow eng-sre oncall escalation documented in: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-escalation.\\n\\nChange log\\n----------\\n- 2026-02-15: initial published draft by Priya Menon.\\n- 2026-03-01: clarified dynamic weighting clipping rules; added default baseline policy.\",\n  \"owner\": null,\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_aca3c58497ec4182b8df9c0d6f2e9f89\"\n}",

  "content": "Overview
=======

Purpose
-------
This document specifies a standard for orchestrating ensemble-style evaluations in Redwood's eval harness. It covers how to configure multi-metric evaluation jobs, how to compute a single acceptance score from heterogeneous metrics, recommended weighting strategies, and the operational rules used for model acceptance, canary rollouts, and automated rollback triggers. The goal is consistent, explainable production decisions across different product use-cases (chat, summarization, reranking, embeddings).

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Teams frequently need to combine multiple eval signals (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE-like n-gram overlap, semantic similarity, safety pass rate, latency percentiles) into a single decision for model promotion or rollback. Without a standard approach:
- teams create ad-hoc weights that are hard to justify
- comparisons across workloads are inconsistent
- drift or slice regressions are missed when only aggregate metrics are considered

Scope
-----
This guide applies to:
- All evaluation jobs run through eval-harness-runner and eval-orch services.
- Post-training checks that feed Redwood Optimize and model-onboarding pipelines.
- Production acceptance gates tied to rollout automation in the deployment orchestration layer.

Terminology
-----------
- eval job: a single run that produces a set of metrics for a model version on a prompt set.
- slice: an orthogonal data subset (e.g., low-resource queries, long-contexts, legal-phrasing).
- metric vector: the set of scalar metrics produced by one eval job.
- ensemble score: a normalized, weighted aggregation of metrics used for acceptance decisions.

High-level orchestration
-----------------------
1) Eval job submission: developers submit an eval job YAML to eval-orch. Jobs declare model id, dataset id, slices, metrics, and desired aggregations.
2) Parallel runners: eval-harness-runner scales horizontally to execute slices in parallel. Per-slice results are written to metric-store with a unique job id.
3) Post-processing: a standardized post-processing step normalizes raw metrics, computes slice-level z-scores or bounded transforms, and produces the ensemble score.
4) Decision hooks: the ensemble score is compared against the configured acceptance matrix (thresholds and weights). If the score passes, the model progresses to canary rollout; otherwise it triggers triage.

Orchestration diagram (text)
---------------------------
- user -> eval-orch -> queue (kafka) -> runner pool -> metric-store (timeseries + artifacts) -> postproc -> decision-service -> deployment-orch

Weighting and aggregation strategies
----------------------------------
We provide three canonical strategies. Choose the simplest that satisfies your product requirements; prefer reproducibility over complexity.

1) Equal-weight normalized aggregation (default)
- Use when metrics are commensurate after normalization (e.g., all are percentages or bounded scores).
- Steps: compute per-metric min/max clipped to historical percentiles (5th/95th), rescale to [0,1], average.
- Pros: simple, transparent.
- Cons: can under- or over-emphasize rare but critical metrics.

2) Priority-weighted aggregation
- Use when one metric is safety-critical (e.g., toxicity, hallucination rate).
- Steps: assign integer priority weights (example: safety=5, accuracy=3, latency=1), normalize weights to sum to 1, compute weighted sum of normalized metrics.
- Documentation: every priority weight must have an author and justification recorded in the eval job metadata.

3) Dynamic frequency-weighted aggregation (recommended for customer-facing embeddings/reranking)
- Use when production slice frequencies differ significantly from training/test distributions.
- Steps: estimate slice frequencies from production telemetry (last 30 days), compute per-slice weight proportional to frequency, and combine slice-level metric aggregates into a global metric before normalization.
- Important: frequency estimates are clipped to [0.01, 0.5] per slice to avoid domination by a single slice.

Normalization and transforms
---------------------------
We standardize on the following transforms before aggregation:
- bounded metrics in [0,1] (no transform)
- unbounded error metrics (e.g., MSE): apply inverse transform 1/(1+log(1+value)) then rescale to [0,1]
- latency percentiles: map P50/P95 to score = 1 - min(latency / latency_slo, 1) (SLOs stored in product-config)
- safety/failure rates: use 1 - rate so higher is better
- For metrics with heavy tails, use winsorization at 99th percentile prior to normalization

Scoring formula (canonical)
--------------------------
Given normalized metrics m_i in [0,1] and weights w_i that sum to 1:
ensemble_score = sum_i w_i * m_i

When combining slices, compute slice_score_j first (per-slice aggregation across metrics), then global_score = sum_j slice_weight_j * slice_score_j where slice_weight_j is chosen per weighting strategy.

Config examples
--------------
Example eval job YAML (submit to eval-orch):

---
job_name: "chat-v2-ensemble-eval"
model_id: "m-redwood-chat-v2-2026-03"
dataset_id: "chat-production-sim-2026-01"
metrics: ["semantic-similarity", "toxicity_rate", "response_length_variance", "p95_latency_ms"]
slices: ["all", "long_context_>2048", "low_english_proficiency"]
weighting_strategy: "dynamic-frequency"
weights: {} # optional for dynamic; required for priority-weighted
postproc:
  normalization: "percentile-clip-5-95"
  latency_slo_ms: 150
notify_on_fail: ["ml-evals@redwoodeval.internal"]
---

Example postproc snippet (pseudo-YAML) for priority-weighted:

weights:
  semantic-similarity: 0.4
  toxicity_rate: 0.4
  p95_latency_ms: 0.2
normalization: "1/(1+log(1+value))"

Acceptance matrix and thresholds
--------------------------------
Acceptance matrices must be checked into model-onboarding metadata and include:
- minimum safety pass rate by slice (e.g., safety >= 0.995 on all slices),
- global ensemble_score threshold (default 0.82),
- latency SLO tolerances (P95 <= configured SLO),
- allowed per-metric regressions from baseline (e.g., no more than 2% drop in semantic-similarity).

Default baseline policy (applies if team does not provide custom matrix):
- safety pass rate >= 0.998 on all slices
- ensemble_score >= 0.80
- no metric regressions > 3% compared to production baseline
- canary rollout limited to 5% traffic for 48 hours with monitoring hooks

Canary and rollback rules
------------------------
Canary rollout: on pass, deployment-orch will deploy model to canary cluster at 5% traffic. During canary the following automated checks run every 15 minutes:
- Production sampler run: compare online metrics with eval predictions for a random sample of requests (1 per 1000 requests or at least 1000 samples/day).
- Alert conditions: ensemble_score drop > 0.05 vs baseline OR safety failure spike > 0.01 absolute OR P95 latency increase > 25% -> trigger rollback.

Automated rollback sequence (executed by deployment-orch):
1) Pause canary traffic.
2) Demote model from canary and switch traffic to previous stable model.
3) Create incident and assign to on-call owner of model-service (see runbooks).
4) Persist failing eval artifacts and logs under job id for triage.

Regression triage flow
---------------------
1) Triage owner reviews per-slice deltas and pulls failing examples (eval-harness provides direct links).
2) If failure is dataset-related (label drift), tag dataset and schedule augmentation.
3) If failure is model-related (systematic hallucination/safety), open ModelRegression ticket with: baseline artifacts, counterexamples, per-slice metrics, and suggested mitigation (prompt tuning, quantization rollback, smaller context window).
4) For performance regressions, check runtime config (quantization profile, batching settings) and revert to last-known-good profile if needed.

Operational considerations and do's/don'ts
----------------------------------------
Do:
- Record weight justifications in job metadata.
- Use production frequency data for dynamic weighting when available.
- Always include safety metrics as separate slices (do not absorb safety into a single aggregate without explicit weight).
- Keep acceptance matrices in model-onboarding for auditability.
Don't:
- Hard-code weights in deployment scripts without provenance.
- Use raw latency numbers directly without mapping to SLO-based scores.
- Rely solely on aggregate scores; always require per-slice checks for safety and critical business slices.

Metrics and observability
------------------------
- metric-store: stores per-job, per-slice metrics with job_id and model_id tags.
- dashboards: ensemble-over-time, per-slice-breakdown, canary-sampler-comparison.
- alerts: configured in deployment-orch and routed to ml-evals and eng-sre channels.

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Eval orchestration (eval-orch, runner): team = applied-ml (owner: Priya Menon).
- Post-processing & scoring library: team = applied-ml, SLAs for processing of a single job <= 30 minutes for medium datasets (<=100k examples).
- Decision-service and deployment hooks: team = eng-platform.

Required artifacts for onboarding a new model using ensemble evals
----------------------------------------------------------------
- eval job YAML and historical weight justifications (checked into model PR)
- acceptance matrix (JSON) checked into model-onboarding metadata store
- baseline production metrics snapshot (timestamped)
- list of critical slices and slice definitions

Appendix: example of normalized score calculations
------------------------------------------------
Given metrics: semantic_sim=0.78 (higher better), toxicity_rate=0.002 (lower better), p95_latency_ms=120 (SLO=150)
Transform toxicity: 1 - toxicity_rate = 0.998
Transform latency: 1 - min(120/150, 1) = 0.2
Assume weights [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] -> ensemble_score = 0.5*0.78 + 0.3*0.998 + 0.2*0.2 = 0.39 + 0.2994 + 0.04 = 0.7294

Links and references
--------------------
- eval-harness-runner README: internal link (eval-harness-runner)
- model-onboarding checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/production-model-certification-checklist-2026
- regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026

Contact and escalation
----------------------
For questions about weighting strategy or to request new slice definitions, open an issue in the Applied-ML backlog and assign to the evals owner (Priya Menon). For production incidents related to canary rollouts, follow eng-sre oncall escalation documented in: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-escalation.

Change log
----------
- 2026-02-15: initial published draft by Priya Menon.
- 2026-03-01: clarified dynamic weighting clipping rules; added default baseline policy.",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-46812\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Statistical validation suite for embedding + rerank regression detection\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"creator\": \"Maya Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Jonah Reyes\",\n  \"project\": \"embeddings-eval-suite\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-04-01\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"reranking\",\n    \"drift-detection\",\n    \"offline-metrics\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-41722\",\n    \"ENG-25467\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.22\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Build a statistically-grounded validation suite that produces daily quality scorecards for embedding and reranking endpoints, surfaces regressions with confidence intervals, and integrates with alerting and PR workflows. This suite will combine curated human-labeled corpora, stratified sampling for latency buckets, synthetic perturbations, and time-series drift detectors. Outputs: nightly scorecards, auto-created incidents when metric regressions exceed thresholds, and a small lightweight CLI to run local quickchecks before merging embedding/rerank model changes.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Nightly job produces a JSON scorecard with at least these metrics: MRR@10, nDCG@10, precision@1, recall@K, embedding distance calibration (cosine shift), and paired-significance p-value between current and baseline.\",\n    \"Scorecard includes latency stratification: p50/p90 token generation and end-to-end rerank latency per shard.\",\n    \"Automated alerts defined: threshold-based (absolute) and regression-based (relative with bootstrap CI) that create a ticket and post to #infra-embeddings when triggered.\",\n    \"CLI 'embed-validate quickcheck' runs a 200-sample smoke test in under 2 minutes and returns pass/fail and simple diffs for top-k rerank outputs.\",\n    \"Integration with PR process: a GitHub check that runs the quickcheck and attaches the scorecard link when embeddings/rerank config files change.\",\n    \"Dashboard in Console that shows historical metrics and drift decomposition by dataset slice and latency bucket.\",\n    \"Runbook for on-call: explanation of common false positives, how to rebaseline goldset, and steps to roll back model variants to a fallback.\",\n    \"Documentation page in Confluence with dataset stewardship guidelines and labeling rubric.\",\n    \"End-to-end tests for the nightly pipeline and a small synthetic perturbation suite to validate detectors.\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_plan\": [\n    \"Phase 1: Build canonical scorecard schema and nightly runner (batch Spark job -> scoring service) using existing embedding eval infra as a base.\",\n    \"Phase 2: Curate validation corpora: (a) small human-verified core set (2000 queries across domains), (b) stratified latency slices from production traces, (c) synthetic perturbation generators (typos, paraphrases, adversarial negation).\",\n    \"Phase 3: Instrument rerank endpoints to capture top-k outputs and token-latencies for sampled requests; store samples in S3 with tags for slice and model-variant.\",\n    \"Phase 4: Implement statistical tests: bootstrap CI for mean differences, paired Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney when appropriate, and Kendall/MRR correlation checks for rerank stability.\",\n    \"Phase 5: Alerting and automation: implement regression-detector lambda that compares yesterday vs baseline window and opens ENG tickets + posts Slack alerts. Integrate with GitHub checks for pre-merge quickchecks.\",\n    \"Phase 6: Observability and UX: Console dashboard + downloadable scorecard JSONs for auditors; add endpoints for programmatic polling (read-only).\",\n    \"Phase 7: Run internal pilot with two product teams for one month, iterate thresholds and onboarding docs, then promote to default nightly run for all embedding/rerank models.\"\n  ],\n  \"technical_considerations\": [\n    \"Sampling strategy must be cost-aware: use reservoir sampling on production traces to keep required sample set under budgeted S3/compute cost.\",\n    \"Latency-aware slices: bucket samples by observed inference p50/p90 to detect quality-latency tradeoffs introduced by new quantized variants.\",\n    \"Baseline management: support rolling baselines (30-day window) and per-model pinned baselines for release blockers.\",\n    \"False positive mitigation: require both absolute drop and statistically significant paired test before auto-creating high-priority incidents.\",\n    \"Data retention and PII: sampled request payloads must be redacted and follow Private deployment policy; store only tokens + hashed identifiers where necessary.\",\n    \"Performance: nightly job must complete within the 2-hour nightly window; quickcheck must be sub-2 minutes for developer feedback loop.\",\n    \"Cost: estimate additional monthly S3 + compute ~ $1.5k for the core suite initially; include budget in the infra cost center.\"\n  ],\n  \"risks_and_mitigation\": [\n    \"Risk: Over-alerting on minor variance leads to alert fatigue. Mitigation: use sliding windows and require CI overlap test before raising P1s.\",\n    \"Risk: Goldset stale or biased. Mitigation: implement quarterly goldset review with labelers and rotate in fresh queries from production sampling.\",\n    \"Risk: Increased storage and compute cost. Mitigation: aggressive retention policy and ability to downsample older runs to aggregated statistics only.\",\n    \"Risk: Inconsistent measurements across dedicated vs hosted. Mitigation: include environment tags and require separate baselines per deployment mode.\"\n  ],\n  \"deliverables\": [\n    \"Scorecard schema and nightly runner in repo 'infra/embed-eval'.\",\n    \"Embed-validate CLI with quickcheck command in 'tools/embed-validate'.\",\n    \"Console dashboard with historical graphs and dataset slice filters.\",\n    \"GitHub check integration and example workflow for PRs modifying models/config.\",\n    \"Confluence doc: 'Embedding & Rerank Validation Playbook' with stewarding guidelines.\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-01-12 - Maya Patel: Initial spike completed. Prototype scorecard schema in /repos/infra/embed-eval/schema/v1.json. Found that MRR variance is high on tail-heavy datasets.\",\n    \"2026-01-25 - Jonah Reyes: PoC runner done. It samples 5k requests from traces and computes MRR/nDCG. Needs latency tagging and CI computations.\",\n    \"2026-02-02 - Elisa Gomez (Data Science): Suggested adding stratified bootstrap to handle heavy-tailed relevance scores; shared notebook Gist: gist.github.com/elisa/stratified-bootstrap.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 - Jonah Reyes: PR 241 on GitHub opens for CLI quickcheck (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/241). Running quickcheck in CI has ~90s runtime on small samples.\",\n    \"2026-03-01 - Product review: PM Neil Chang requested a dashboard tile showing model-impact-by-customer-tier. We'll add a customer_tier slice to the scorecard.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 - Security: small note to ensure sampled request redaction for Private customers. Added retention plan and redaction checklist to the Confluence doc.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 - Jonah Reyes: Nightly runner scheduled in Airflow; first nightly run succeeded. Observed a small regression on a paraphrase-heavy slice; alert created and labeled P2 for triage.\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Validation+Playbook\",\n    \"GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/241\",\n    \"Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/embed-scorecard-proto\",\n    \"Notebook (analysis): https://gist.github.com/elisa/stratified-bootstrap\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"implementation_plan\",\n    \"technical_considerations\",\n    \"risks_and_mitigation\",\n    \"deliverables\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_055e17a2e9ad484b9aaef11f95ed2eeb\"\n}",

document.title: Statistical validation suite for embedding + rerank regression detection
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-46812",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Statistical validation suite for embedding + rerank regression detection",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-01-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-12",
  "creator": "Maya Patel",
  "assignee": "Jonah Reyes",
  "project": "embeddings-eval-suite",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-04-01",
  "labels": [
    "embeddings",
    "reranking",
    "drift-detection",
    "offline-metrics",
    "telemetry"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-41722",
    "ENG-25467"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "runtime-1.22",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Build a statistically-grounded validation suite that produces daily quality scorecards for embedding and reranking endpoints, surfaces regressions with confidence intervals, and integrates with alerting and PR workflows. This suite will combine curated human-labeled corpora, stratified sampling for latency buckets, synthetic perturbations, and time-series drift detectors. Outputs: nightly scorecards, auto-created incidents when metric regressions exceed thresholds, and a small lightweight CLI to run local quickchecks before merging embedding/rerank model changes.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Nightly job produces a JSON scorecard with at least these metrics: MRR@10, nDCG@10, precision@1, recall@K, embedding distance calibration (cosine shift), and paired-significance p-value between current and baseline.",
    "Scorecard includes latency stratification: p50/p90 token generation and end-to-end rerank latency per shard.",
    "Automated alerts defined: threshold-based (absolute) and regression-based (relative with bootstrap CI) that create a ticket and post to #infra-embeddings when triggered.",
    "CLI 'embed-validate quickcheck' runs a 200-sample smoke test in under 2 minutes and returns pass/fail and simple diffs for top-k rerank outputs.",
    "Integration with PR process: a GitHub check that runs the quickcheck and attaches the scorecard link when embeddings/rerank config files change.",
    "Dashboard in Console that shows historical metrics and drift decomposition by dataset slice and latency bucket.",
    "Runbook for on-call: explanation of common false positives, how to rebaseline goldset, and steps to roll back model variants to a fallback.",
    "Documentation page in Confluence with dataset stewardship guidelines and labeling rubric.",
    "End-to-end tests for the nightly pipeline and a small synthetic perturbation suite to validate detectors."
  ],
  "implementation_plan": [
    "Phase 1: Build canonical scorecard schema and nightly runner (batch Spark job -> scoring service) using existing embedding eval infra as a base.",
    "Phase 2: Curate validation corpora: (a) small human-verified core set (2000 queries across domains), (b) stratified latency slices from production traces, (c) synthetic perturbation generators (typos, paraphrases, adversarial negation).",
    "Phase 3: Instrument rerank endpoints to capture top-k outputs and token-latencies for sampled requests; store samples in S3 with tags for slice and model-variant.",
    "Phase 4: Implement statistical tests: bootstrap CI for mean differences, paired Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney when appropriate, and Kendall/MRR correlation checks for rerank stability.",
    "Phase 5: Alerting and automation: implement regression-detector lambda that compares yesterday vs baseline window and opens ENG tickets + posts Slack alerts. Integrate with GitHub checks for pre-merge quickchecks.",
    "Phase 6: Observability and UX: Console dashboard + downloadable scorecard JSONs for auditors; add endpoints for programmatic polling (read-only).",
    "Phase 7: Run internal pilot with two product teams for one month, iterate thresholds and onboarding docs, then promote to default nightly run for all embedding/rerank models."
  ],
  "technical_considerations": [
    "Sampling strategy must be cost-aware: use reservoir sampling on production traces to keep required sample set under budgeted S3/compute cost.",
    "Latency-aware slices: bucket samples by observed inference p50/p90 to detect quality-latency tradeoffs introduced by new quantized variants.",
    "Baseline management: support rolling baselines (30-day window) and per-model pinned baselines for release blockers.",
    "False positive mitigation: require both absolute drop and statistically significant paired test before auto-creating high-priority incidents.",
    "Data retention and PII: sampled request payloads must be redacted and follow Private deployment policy; store only tokens + hashed identifiers where necessary.",
    "Performance: nightly job must complete within the 2-hour nightly window; quickcheck must be sub-2 minutes for developer feedback loop.",
    "Cost: estimate additional monthly S3 + compute ~ $1.5k for the core suite initially; include budget in the infra cost center."
  ],
  "risks_and_mitigation": [
    "Risk: Over-alerting on minor variance leads to alert fatigue. Mitigation: use sliding windows and require CI overlap test before raising P1s.",
    "Risk: Goldset stale or biased. Mitigation: implement quarterly goldset review with labelers and rotate in fresh queries from production sampling.",
    "Risk: Increased storage and compute cost. Mitigation: aggressive retention policy and ability to downsample older runs to aggregated statistics only.",
    "Risk: Inconsistent measurements across dedicated vs hosted. Mitigation: include environment tags and require separate baselines per deployment mode."
  ],
  "deliverables": [
    "Scorecard schema and nightly runner in repo 'infra/embed-eval'.",
    "Embed-validate CLI with quickcheck command in 'tools/embed-validate'.",
    "Console dashboard with historical graphs and dataset slice filters.",
    "GitHub check integration and example workflow for PRs modifying models/config.",
    "Confluence doc: 'Embedding & Rerank Validation Playbook' with stewarding guidelines."
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-01-12 - Maya Patel: Initial spike completed. Prototype scorecard schema in /repos/infra/embed-eval/schema/v1.json. Found that MRR variance is high on tail-heavy datasets.",
    "2026-01-25 - Jonah Reyes: PoC runner done. It samples 5k requests from traces and computes MRR/nDCG. Needs latency tagging and CI computations.",
    "2026-02-02 - Elisa Gomez (Data Science): Suggested adding stratified bootstrap to handle heavy-tailed relevance scores; shared notebook Gist: gist.github.com/elisa/stratified-bootstrap.",
    "2026-02-18 - Jonah Reyes: PR 241 on GitHub opens for CLI quickcheck (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/241). Running quickcheck in CI has ~90s runtime on small samples.",
    "2026-03-01 - Product review: PM Neil Chang requested a dashboard tile showing model-impact-by-customer-tier. We'll add a customer_tier slice to the scorecard.",
    "2026-03-10 - Security: small note to ensure sampled request redaction for Private customers. Added retention plan and redaction checklist to the Confluence doc.",
    "2026-03-12 - Jonah Reyes: Nightly runner scheduled in Airflow; first nightly run succeeded. Observed a small regression on a paraphrase-heavy slice; alert created and labeled P2 for triage."
  ],
  "links": [
    "Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Validation+Playbook",
    "GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/241",
    "Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/embed-scorecard-proto",
    "Notebook (analysis): https://gist.github.com/elisa/stratified-bootstrap"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "implementation_plan",
    "technical_considerations",
    "risks_and_mitigation",
    "deliverables",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_055e17a2e9ad484b9aaef11f95ed2eeb"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_a623969386584df59c1156cd9136015b",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/github/eval-harness/pr-243190-add-coverage-weighted-eval-harness-and-stable-delta-reporter.json",
    "title": "Add coverage-weighted evaluation harness and stable-delta reporter",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"eval-harness\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"243190\",\n  \"title\": \"Add coverage-weighted evaluation harness and stable-delta reporter\",\n  \"author\": \"Asha Patel\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-01-28\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-02-10\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2025-02-10\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/coverage-weighted-reporter\",\n  \"description\": \"Context and motivation: Our existing CI gating uses aggregate metrics that treat every prompt equally which underweights long-tail coverage issues and makes small distributional shifts noisy. This PR introduces a coverage-weighted evaluation harness and a stable-delta reporter to (1) surface regressions concentrated in undercovered prompt cohorts, (2) reduce false positives from high-variance short cohorts, and (3) provide a compact delta artifact for CI that is robust to nondeterministic seeds. The description below summarizes design, changes, and operational notes.\\n\\nWhat this delivers: coverage-weighted scoring: per-prompt weights derived from historical sample counts and semantic-diversity scores; cohort-aware aggregation that downweights unstable micro-cohorts; stable-delta reporter: deterministic summarization of before/after evals using bootstrap-smoothed deltas + significance bucketing; a small integration layer and a CI reporter that emits a machine-parsable artifact for the PR pipeline.\\n\\nChecklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1145) [x] unit tests for weighting logic [x] e2e smoke pipeline runs in CI [x] docs/guide for teams to adopt the reporter [x] added metrics and trace spans for debugging\\n\\nCommits summary: - 9 commits: initial weighting algorithm + tests; add bootstrap smoothing utils; implement stable-delta reporter CLI; wire into github CI reporter; add semantic-diversity scorer (fast, approximate); docs and examples; refactor eval runner to accept optional weight maps; fix edge-case on zero-count cohorts; final test fixes and plugin registration.\\n\\nChanged areas (high level): - eval_harness/core/weighting.py: new weighting primitives and heuristics for coverage and diversity - eval_harness/reporting/stable_delta.py: new reporter that produces compact JSON deltas and human summary - eval_harness/cli/report_ci.py: CI entrypoint to run targeted evals and emit artifacts - tests/unit/test_weighting.py, tests/integration/test_stable_delta_end_to_end.py - docs/guides/coverage_weighting.md - examples/coverage_demo/prompt_set.yaml\\n\\nOperational notes: The weighting defaults are conservative (weight floor 0.02) so small cohorts are visible but cannot dominate the aggregated score. The stable-delta reporter outputs both a human-readable summary and a compressed artifact (.json.gz) that CI uploads as an artifact. The reporter includes a deterministic seed and a small bootstrap sweep (default 50 resamples) to smooth noisy per-prompt metrics; runtime overhead observed in smoke runs: ~6% extra time for 2k prompt sets on a 16-core worker.\\n\\nCI run summary: First CI run failed style/lint on one minor import ordering; subsequent runs passed all checks including unit tests and integration smoke. The PR attaches the CI artifact for the final successful run.\\n\\nMerge notes: After two approvals and one small follow-up hotfix to doc wording, this PR was squash-merged into main. document.title: Add coverage-weighted evaluation harness and stable-delta reporter
document.content:
{
  "repo": "eval-harness",
  "pr_number": "243190",
  "title": "Add coverage-weighted evaluation harness and stable-delta reporter",
  "author": "Asha Patel",
  "created_at": "2025-01-28",
  "updated_at": "2025-02-10",
  "merged_at": "2025-02-10",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/coverage-weighted-reporter",
  "description": "Context and motivation: Our existing CI gating uses aggregate metrics that treat every prompt equally which underweights long-tail coverage issues and makes small distributional shifts noisy. This PR introduces a coverage-weighted evaluation harness and a stable-delta reporter to (1) surface regressions concentrated in undercovered prompt cohorts, (2) reduce false positives from high-variance short cohorts, and (3) provide a compact delta artifact for CI that is robust to nondeterministic seeds. The description below summarizes design, changes, and operational notes.\n\nWhat this delivers: coverage-weighted scoring: per-prompt weights derived from historical sample counts and semantic-diversity scores; cohort-aware aggregation that downweights unstable micro-cohorts; stable-delta reporter: deterministic summarization of before/after evals using bootstrap-smoothed deltas + significance bucketing; a small integration layer and a CI reporter that emits a machine-parsable artifact for the PR pipeline.\n\nChecklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1145) [x] unit tests for weighting logic [x] e2e smoke pipeline runs in CI [x] docs/guide for teams to adopt the reporter [x] added metrics and trace spans for debugging\n\nCommits summary: - 9 commits: initial weighting algorithm + tests; add bootstrap smoothing utils; implement stable-delta reporter CLI; wire into github CI reporter; add semantic-diversity scorer (fast, approximate); docs and examples; refactor eval runner to accept optional weight maps; fix edge-case on zero-count cohorts; final test fixes and plugin registration.\n\nChanged areas (high level): - eval_harness/core/weighting.py: new weighting primitives and heuristics for coverage and diversity - eval_harness/reporting/stable_delta.py: new reporter that produces compact JSON deltas and human summary - eval_harness/cli/report_ci.py: CI entrypoint to run targeted evals and emit artifacts - tests/unit/test_weighting.py, tests/integration/test_stable_delta_end_to_end.py - docs/guides/coverage_weighting.md - examples/coverage_demo/prompt_set.yaml\n\nOperational notes: The weighting defaults are conservative (weight floor 0.02) so small cohorts are visible but cannot dominate the aggregated score. The stable-delta reporter outputs both a human-readable summary and a compressed artifact (.json.gz) that CI uploads as an artifact. The reporter includes a deterministic seed and a small bootstrap sweep (default 50 resamples) to smooth noisy per-prompt metrics; runtime overhead observed in smoke runs: ~6% extra time for 2k prompt sets on a 16-core worker.\n\nCI run summary: First CI run failed style/lint on one minor import ordering; subsequent runs passed all checks including unit tests and integration smoke. The PR attaches the CI artifact for the final successful run.\n\nMerge notes: After two approvals and one small follow-up hotfix to doc wording, this PR was squash-merged into main. Release notes include a short adoption guide and recommended defaults.\n\nReferences: Linear ENG-1145 (Coverage-weighted eval prototype), PM-321 (QA gating for prompt-sets).",
  "commits": [
    "Initial coverage-weighting primitives and tests",
    "Add semantic-diversity fast scorer (approximate) and benchmarks",
    "Bootstrap-smoothed delta utilities",
    "Stable-delta reporter CLI and JSON artifact format",
    "Integrate reporter into CI reporter step",
    "Refactor eval runner to accept weight maps",
    "Add unit and integration tests",
    "Docs: guide and adoption examples",
    "Fix: zero-count cohort edge-case and test flakiness"
  ],
  "changed_files": [
    "eval_harness/core/weighting.py",
    "eval_harness/reporting/stable_delta.py",
    "eval_harness/cli/report_ci.py",
    "tests/unit/test_weighting.py",
    "tests/integration/test_stable_delta_end_to_end.py",
    "docs/guides/coverage_weighting.md",
    "examples/coverage_demo/prompt_set.yaml",
    "setup.cfg",
    "pyproject.toml"
  ],
  "reviewers": [
    "Lina Chen",
    "Omar Karim",
    "Priya Nair"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "eval",
    "ci",
    "metrics",
    "feature",
    "perf"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-1145",
    "PM-321"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "SUP-907"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "9",
  "additions": "652",
  "deletions": "128",
  "release_notes": "Adds coverage-weighted eval aggregation and a stable-delta CI reporter. Teams can opt-in by providing a weight map or using the default heuristic; recommended for prompt sets with long-tail cohorts.",
  "merge_method": "squash",
  "review_comments": [
    "Lina Chen: Overall LGTM; left a couple questions about the default floor and the impact on existing dashboards.",
    "Omar Karim: Proposed a small refactor to avoid recomputing semantic-diversity for repeated runs; suggested memoization in the scorer.",
    "Priya Nair: Confirmed artifacts and integration with the CI uploader; requested a short how-to in docs for using the artifact in release notes.",
    "Author (Asha Patel): Addressed import ordering lint, added memoization cache with TTL, expanded docs with example pipeline snippet; replied to reviewers with benchmark numbers."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "commits",
    "review_comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_a623969386584df59c1156cd9136015b"
}

item.aggregated_output: # Agent Guidelines for Langfuse Langfuse is an open source LLM engineering platform for developing, monitoring, evaluating, and debugging AI applications. ## How To Work - Read the minimal local context required for the task. - Keep changes scoped and avoid unrelated refactors. - If you are about to write a `useEffect` — or sync fetched data into state, or wire form initial values from loaded data — read `.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md` first. Most such effects should not exist. - For bug fixes, write the failing test first, confirm it fails, then fix the bug. If the bug depends on a data shape, pause and ask: can `pnpm run seed` prefill that shape locally? If not, consider extending a seeder scenario so the bug stays cheaply reproducible (`packages/shared/scripts/seeder/AGENTS.md`), or note why a seed cannot express it. - For user-visible frontend changes in `web/**`, review the affected flow in a real browser before signoff. Prefill the data the flow needs with the seed CLI (`pnpm run seed -- list` shows scenarios; runs print UI deep links) — never with ad-hoc scripts or raw ClickHouse inserts. - When fixing an isolated styling issue in an individual component, read `.agents/skills/storybook/SKILL.md` create or update a component story following its guidance first. - Every PR auto-builds (via GitHub Actions) a disposable, full-stack preview at `pr-.preview.langfuse.com` — nothing to spin up. Use the `langfuse-previews` skill to use or debug one, e.g. read a preview's web/worker error logs with `kubectl`. - For documentation screenshots in Markdown, avoid fixed `height` on `` tags; prefer Markdown images or width-only HTML so previews preserve aspect ratio. - When working on the search bar or any filtering UI/grammar, read `web/src/features/search-bar/README.md` first. It owns the grammar ↔ `FilterState` contract, the validate/lower parity invariants, and the cross-view extension playbook — the bar is intended to become the primary filter interface for every filterable view, so new filtering work extends it through that contract rather than forking it. - When adding or modifying any chart, dashboard, or chart formatter, read `web/src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md` first — the charts manifesto. It owns the data → preparer → visualiser contract: presentation decisions live in the preparer, not the chart components. - Do not add or widen ESLint disable comments or config overrides without explicit user approval for the exact rule and scope. - Always quote file paths in shell commands, or use `noglob` for path-heavy commands, to avoid zsh glob expansion issues with dynamic Next.js routes. - Never invoke Node-installed binaries through `./node_modules/.bin/*`. Always run them through `pnpm`. - Never commit secrets or credentials. Keep `.env*.example` files in sync with required env vars. ## Project Structure ```text langfuse/ |- web/ # Next.js app (UI + tRPC + public REST) |- worker/ # Queue consumers and background processing |- packages/shared/ # Shared domain, DB, queue contracts, repositories |- ee/ # Enterprise package consumed by web |- generated/ # Generated API clients (do not hand-edit) |- fern/ # API definition sources `- scripts/ # Repo scripts ``` - Dependency direction: - `web` -> `@langfuse/shared`, `@langfuse/ee` - `worker` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/ee` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/shared` -> no imports from `web`, `worker`, or `ee` - Queue payload schemas and queue-name contracts are owned by `packages/shared/src/server/queues.ts`. - High-signal shared entry points: - Domain models: `packages/shared/src/domain/{observations,traces,scores}.ts` - Postgres schema: `packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma` - ClickHouse migrations: `packages/shared/clickhouse/migrations/{clustered,unclustered}/*.sql` - Architecture principles live in `.agents/ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES.md`. ## Core Commands - Install deps: `pnpm install` - Dev all packages: `pnpm run dev` - Dev web only: `pnpm run dev:web` - Dev worker only: `pnpm run dev:worker` - Lint all: `pnpm run lint` - Typecheck all: `pnpm run typecheck` / `pnpm tc` - Run a single test file (vitest filters on the filename argument): - web server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test ` (client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client `) - worker: `pnpm --filter worker run test ` - shared: `pnpm --filter @langfuse/shared run test ` - Build check: `pnpm run build:check` - Full build: `pnpm run build` - Worktree bootstrap: `bash scripts/codex/setup.sh` - Worktree maintenance: `bash scripts/codex/maintenance.sh` - Install Playwright Chromium: `pnpm run playwright:install` ## Local Data Inspection - For feature testing and debugging, inspect the local databases directly when it helps you understand the existing test data. Prefer read-only queries, and continue to use the seed CLI to create frontend test state rather than ad-hoc inserts. - Dev Docker Compose exposes these clients on `${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}`: - Postgres: `PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres}" psql -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5432}" -U "${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}" -d "${POSTGRES_DB:-postgres}"` - ClickHouse: `clickhouse client --host "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" --port "${CLICKHOUSE_NATIVE_PORT:-9000}" --user "${CLICKHOUSE_USER:-clickhouse}" --password "${CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD:-clickhouse}" --database default` - Redis: `REDISCLI_AUTH="${REDIS_AUTH:-myredissecret}" redis-cli -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${REDIS_HOST_PORT:-6379}"` - If any connection fails, check `docker-compose.dev.yml` for local override variables and confirm the services are running. ## Verification - `web/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted web tests. - `worker/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted worker tests. - `packages/shared/**` non-schema changes: `pnpm run lint` plus one targeted web check and one targeted worker check. - `packages/shared/prisma/**` or `packages/shared/clickhouse/**`: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run db:generate`, and targeted web/worker regressions. - Public API contracts in `web/src/pages/api/public/**`, `web/src/features/public-api/types/**`, or `fern/apis/**`: `pnpm run lint`, targeted server API tests, and Fern update/regeneration. - Cross-package refactors: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and targeted tests for impacted packages. - Client-bundle soundness: CI scans every prod web build (`pnpm run scan:client-bundle`) for minifier-dropped bindings and Node-only globals leaking into browser chunks — the SWC dropped-binding class ships runtime-only `ReferenceError`s that dev builds and type checks cannot see (LFE-10645). On failure, `scripts/scan-client-bundle.mjs`'s header explains the canonical fix. End your turn with evidence, not claims: quote each check's summary line — e.g. `Tasks: 8 successful, 8 total` (turbo lint/typecheck) or `Tests 12 passed (12)` (vitest) — say which checks you skipped and why, never report unverified work as done, and never end with work pending. ## Generated Files Do not hand-edit generated or build artifacts: - `generated/*` - `web/.next/*` - `web/.next-check/*` - `*/dist/*` - `packages/shared/prisma/generated/*` Public API contract changes must update Fern sources in `fern/apis/**` and regenerated outputs. Never hand-edit `generated/**`. ## Shared Agent Setup - `.agents/AGENTS.md` is the canonical root guide. - Root `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `.agents/AGENTS.md`. - Root `CLAUDE.md` is a compatibility symlink to `AGENTS.md`. - When creating or editing `.agents/skills/**`, use `.agents/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md`; keep skills concise with progressive disclosure. - After changing shared agent setup, run `pnpm run agents:sync` and `pnpm run agents:check`. - Generated provider config and shim outputs under `.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.codex/`, `.vscode/`, or `.mcp.json` are local artifacts, not source of truth files. # Codex Guidelines for `web` This file covers package-local guidance for this package. Use root [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for monorepo-level rules. ## Purpose - Next.js application with UI, tRPC backend, and public REST API routes. - Check `web/package.json` for current Next.js, React, and tRPC versions before version-sensitive work. - Primary package for frontend and most request/response surface changes. ## Maintenance Contract - `AGENTS.md` is a living document. - Update this file in the same PR when material web-local changes occur: - new/renamed web entry points - new API route families - changed web-specific verification commands - If the change also affects monorepo workflows or other packages, update root `AGENTS.md` too. ## High-Signal Entry Points - App shell/providers: `src/pages/_app.tsx` - tRPC context/procedures: `src/server/api/trpc.ts` - tRPC router registry: `src/server/api/root.ts` - tRPC routers: `src/server/api/routers/*`, `src/features/*/server/*` - Public REST API routes: `src/pages/api/public/*` - Unstable public eval APIs: `src/pages/api/public/unstable/{evaluators,evaluation-rules}/*` - Feature modules: `src/features/*` - Reusable UI components: `src/components/*` - Tests: - Server integration tests: `src/__tests__/server/*.servertest.ts` - Server unit tests: `src/__tests__/server/unit/*.servertest.ts` - Client tests: `src/**/*.clienttest.ts(x)` - E2E: `src/__e2e__/*` ## Shared Package Imports - Prefer `@langfuse/shared` in frontend-safe web code for shared types, zod schemas, domain contracts, table definitions, prompt/eval/model-pricing helpers, and other cross-runtime utilities. - Use `@langfuse/shared/src/server` only from server-only web code such as `src/server/**`, `src/pages/api/**`, and server tests. - Use `@langfuse/shared/src/db` only in backend or test code that needs direct Prisma access; never route it into client bundles. - Use narrower subpaths such as `@langfuse/shared/src/env` or `@langfuse/shared/encryption` only when that focused surface is the clearest dependency. - See `../packages/shared/AGENTS.md` for the full shared export map and what each entrypoint contains. - For the higher-level platform topology across web, worker, Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis, and S3, also read the architecture handbook: [langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture](https://langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture) with source markdown in `../langfuse-docs/content/handbook/product-engineering/architecture.mdx` (GitHub mirror: [architecture.mdx](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/blob/4188c1ba453240c90a763a8067ef442d68839323/content/handbook/product-engineering/architecture.mdx#L4)). ## Package-Local Skills - Shared browser-review workflow for user-visible frontend changes: [`../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md) - Large frontend feature, virtualized-list, local state, and React effect-free data-flow architecture: [`../.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md) - Avoidable React effect audits, refactors, and module migrations: [`../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md) - React composition and component API design: [`web/.agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md) - React/Next.js performance and rendering best practices: [`web/.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md) - PostHog product analytics — when and how to instrument user actions: [`../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md) - Sentry error capture — whether and how an error path should report: [`../.agents/skills/sentry-instrumentation/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/sentry-instrumentation/SKILL.md) Read these package-local skills before substantial frontend refactors when the task involves component composition, reusable component APIs, rendering performance, virtualized lists, local feature stores, bundle size, React/Next.js performance patterns, or browser-based signoff of user-visible changes. If you are about to write a `useEffect` or wire form initial values from loaded data, read the frontend-large-feature-architecture skill first — most effects that derive or sync state should not exist. When adding a meaningful user action (button, handler, form, mutation, feature surface), read the PostHog instrumentation skill and decide explicitly whether the action should emit an analytics event. When adding or touching an error path — a `captureException` or `console.error` call, an error boundary, a `catch` block, a Worker `onerror`, or a Sentry `beforeSend`/denylist filter — read the Sentry instrumentation skill first and decide whether it should capture at all (and, for any suppression change, answer "does this rule hide a real error?"). ## Web Conventions - **Before adding or modifying a chart, dashboard, or chart formatter, read `src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md` first** — the charts manifesto. It owns the data → preparer → visualiser contract: presentation decisions (formatting, colors, axis scale, overload) live in the preparer, not the chart components. - Put net-new feature code under `src/features//*`; put broadly reusable components under `src/components/*`. - We use tRPC for full-stack web features; register routers in `src/server/api/root.ts`. - Authentication and RBAC guidance lives in `src/features/rbac/README.md`. - Entitlements guidance lives in `src/features/entitlements/README.md`. - Prefer Shadcn/ui primitives from `src/components/ui`; if a missing component must be installed, ask the user before doing so. - When you surface a score in the UI, always show its level (trace/observation/session/experiment) with the `` component (`src/components/score-tag.tsx`) and its global color coding (see the ScoreTag Storybook story). - Tailwind is the default styling layer; use the shared palette and globals in `src/styles/globals.css`. - Do not add `useEffect` by default. Use it only when a component must synchronize with a concrete system outside React, such as a subscription, browser event listener, observer, timer, or imperative third-party API. Before writing an effect, name that external system and its setup/cleanup lifecycle. If there is no external system, do not use an effect. In particular, do not use effects to derive render state, mirror props or query data into local state, react to user actions, or reset state when an ID changes. Derive during render, run work in the initiating event handler, use query APIs for server state, or mount a keyed child once required data is available. Do not evade this rule with `useLayoutEffect`, a custom wrapper hook, an ESLint suppression, or disabled dependency checks. Use `../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md` for effect work. - In flex layouts, prefer `gap-*` over margin-based `space-x-*`/`space-y-*`. - Treat `!` Tailwind classes as a smell. Step back and fix the owning layout, variant, or primitive before overriding with higher specificity. - When changing shared UI/table patterns, update sibling variants consistently, including default-visible and hidden columns or states. - For component style variants, prefer `cva` with `VariantProps` and merge caller classes through `cn`, following existing `src/components/ui/*` components: ```tsx const cardVariants = cva("rounded-md border", { variants: { intent: { default: "bg-background", error: "border-destructive" }, }, defaultVariants: { intent: "default" }, }); type CardProps = React.HTMLAttributes & VariantProps; const className = cn(cardVariants({ intent }), props.className); ``` - When anchoring sticky, fixed, or absolute elements to the viewport, use `top-banner-offset`, `pt-banner-offset`, `h-screen-with-banner`, or `min-h-screen-with-banner` instead of raw `top-0` so banners do not overlap the UI. - **Z-index / layers — key idea: we are migrating from z-indexes to a layer system** (start of a developing design system; extend it, don't work around it). **To put something on top of something else, use a layer, not a z-index.** The app renders inside `#__next`, isolated into one stacking context (`globals.css`), so its z-indexes can't escape; overlays go in layers that sit outside it and always win. `LAYER_ORDER` is `["panel", "agent", "modal", "popover", "tooltip", "toast"]` — containers declared in `_document.tsx`, ordered by that array (later = on top), carrying NO z-index. `panel` is for docked side surfaces like Sheet, Drawer, and the table peek; `modal` is for true blocking Dialog and AlertDialog surfaces. **THE RULE (see `src/components/ui/layer.tsx` JSDoc — source of truth): every overlay portals through a layer container; never let a Radix/Vaul `*.Portal` fall back to ``.** Radix/Vaul primitives route via their `*.Portal`'s `container` (the `ui/*` wrappers do this with `useLayerContainer`); bespoke imperatively-positioned content renders via ``. z-index stays local to a layer or component (1–2 max), never to escape the app — the `@repo/no-overlay-zindex` lint rule enforces it. - **Overlay lifecycle — a dropdown that opens a modal should close first**, not linger under it (a lifecycle bug, not z-order — don't fix it by re-ranking layers). Radix unmounts a Select/DropdownMenu's content on close, so render the Dialog as a SIBLING (trigger inside, dialog outside), as `useAddLlmConnectionSelect` in `src/components/ModelParameters/index.tsx` does (LFE-10615). - Never import `prettier/plugins/typescript` in client code — it embeds the TypeScript compiler, which the SWC minifier miscompiles (dropped bindings → production-only `ReferenceError`; caught by the CI client-bundle scan, LFE-10645). Format TypeScript with `parser: "babel-ts"` + `prettier/plugins/babel` instead, as the eval-template editor does (`src/features/evals/components/code-eval-template-form-body.tsx`). - Public API routes should use `src/features/public-api/server/withMiddlewares.ts`, define strict request and response types in `src/features/public-api/types/*`, add server tests, and update Fern sources when the contract changes. - Public eval endpoints should keep the split between reusable `evaluators` and ingestion-scoped `evaluation-rules`; do not leak `EvalTemplate` or `JobConfiguration` naming into the public contract. - Keep tests independent; in `src/__tests__/server/**`, prefer scoped cleanup or unique test data over global reset helpers. - Put pure server unit tests that do not need Postgres bootstrap under `src/__tests__/server/unit/**` so they skip the shared DB setup hook. - For small utility functions, prefer Vitest in-source tests when colocated coverage is the simplest option, especially when the test needs access to private implementation details without widening the module API. - Do not extract private utility functions into separate files only to make them testable. Keep them local unless the user explicitly asks for extraction or the utility is meaningfully reused. ## Quick Commands - Dev: `pnpm --filter web run dev` - Lint: `pnpm --filter web run lint` - Lint fix: `pnpm --filter web run lint:fix` - Typecheck: `pnpm --filter web run typecheck` - Server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test ` - In-source tests: `pnpm --filter web run test:in-source ` - Client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client ` - E2E tests: `pnpm --filter web run test:e2e` - Agent browser install to the default user-level Playwright cache: `pnpm run playwright:install` - Build: `pnpm --filter web run build` ## Playbooks ### Add/Change tRPC endpoint 1. Implement router/procedure in `src/server/api/routers/*` or `src/features//server/*`. 2. Register in `src/server/api/root.ts`. 3. Reuse auth/error patterns from `src/server/api/trpc.ts`. 4. Add/adjust server tests under `src/__tests__/server/*`. ### Add/Change public API endpoint 1. Add route in `src/pages/api/public/*`. 2. Define/update contract types in `src/features/public-api/types/*`. 3. Add/adjust server tests in `src/__tests__/server/*`. 4. If API contract changed, update Fern source (`../fern/apis/**`) and regenerate outputs (do not hand-edit `../generated/**`). ### Error handling (tRPC + REST) 1. Throw `BaseError` subclasses (eg `LangfuseNotFoundError`) from handlers and services. 2. Let `BaseError`s bubble up to the tRPC and REST middlewares (eg. don't `try/catch` and rethrow in to `TRPCError` the handler) 3. Extend the `BaseError` or its subclasses in [`packages/shared/src/errors/`](../packages/shared/src/errors/) as needed. ### Add frontend feature 1. Prefer `src/features//*` for feature-local code. 2. Put broadly reusable components in `src/components/*`. 3. Keep server logic near feature server folders when possible. 4. For meaningful user actions (buttons, form submits, mode switches), decide explicitly whether to instrument them with PostHog. Use `../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md`. 5. Review the affected user flow in a real browser with the Playwright MCP server before signoff. Use `../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md`. ### Agent browser loop 1. Start the app with `pnpm run dev:web` unless an existing local server is already running. 2. Install Chromium with `pnpm run playwright:install` if Playwright has not been set up on this machine yet. 3. Use the workspace `playwright` MCP server from `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, or `.vscode/mcp.json` for browser-driven review of user-visible frontend changes, not just debugging. 4. Exercise the primary changed flow and check the resulting UI state for obvious visual regressions before signoff. 5. Inspect traces and other artifacts under `/tmp/playwright-mcp` when a browser session fails. ## Package-Specific Rules - Router style is Pages Router-centric; follow existing routing patterns.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -euo pipefail

ensure_env_file() {
  local target_path="$1"
  local fallback_path="$2"

  if [ -f "$target_path" ]; then
    return 0
  fi

  cp "$fallback_path" "$target_path"
}

if ! command -v corepack >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "corepack is required. Use an environment with Node.js 24 support."
  exit 1
fi

corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@11.10.0 --activate

ensure_env_file .env .env.dev.example
ensure_env_file .env.test .env.test.example

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ! docker image inspect "langfuse-in-app-agent-sandbox:latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "packages/in-app-agent-sandbox-runtime/.local-image-built"
  fi

  pnpm turbo run build:docker-image --filter @repo/in-app-agent-sandbox-runtime --output-logs errors-only
else
  echo "Skipping local in-app agent sandbox image build because Docker is not available."
fi

# Install Chromium into the default user-level Playwright cache so frontend
# browser review works on first bootstrap.
pnpm run playwright:install

# Generate the shared Prisma client explicitly in the current worktree before
# the workspace-wide db:generate task, which may be satisfied by Turbo cache.
pnpm --filter=shared run db:generate

# Prisma client generation is needed for typecheck/build tasks.
pnpm run db:generate

arguments.title: Langfuse score analytics histogram and pivot aggregation contracts
arguments.summary: For Langfuse score analytics, histogram bucket membership must be computed from raw numeric values; rounding is presentation-only and label precision must keep adjacent bin edges distinct. Pivot-table avg subtotals and grand totals must be count-weighted when a complete positive count metric is available: sum(group average × group count) / sum(group count). When counts are absent, incomplete, or non-positive, preserve the explicitly tested historical equal-group-average fallback. Non-average aggregations remain unchanged.

When counts are absent, incomplete, or non-positive, preserve the explicitly tested historical equal-group-average fallback. Non-average aggregations remain unchanged.

item.text:
